units.text: # Teleoperators

A teleoperator produces actions for a robot to follow — a leader arm, a gamepad, a keyboard, a phone. All of
them implement the ⟦0⟧ interface, so a recording script written against it works with any input
device.

See [Phone teleoperation](⟦0⟧) and [Isaac Teleop](⟦1⟧) for setup guides, and
[Imitation Learning for Robots](⟦2⟧) for the recording workflow.
## Teleoperator⟦0⟧

⟦0⟧- **config_class** (RobotConfig) -- The expected configuration class for this teleoperator.
- **name** (str) -- The unique name used to identify this teleoperator type.⟦1⟧⟦2⟧
The base abstract class for all LeRobot-compatible teleoperation devices.

This class provides a standardized interface for interacting with physical teleoperators.
Subclasses must implement all abstract methods and properties to be usable.

⟦0⟧- **calibrate** (bool) -- If True, automatically calibrate the teleoperator after connecting if it's not
  calibrated or needs calibration (this is hardware-dependant).⟦1⟧⟦2⟧
Establish communication with the teleoperator.

Apply any one-time or runtime configuration to the teleoperator.
This may include setting motor parameters, control modes, or initial state.
Calibrate the teleoperator if applicable. If not, this should be a no-op.

This method should collect any necessary data (e.g., motor offsets) and update the

A dictionary describing the structure and types of the actions produced by the teleoperator. Its
structure (keys) should match the structure of what is returned by :pymeth:⟦0⟧. Values for
the dict should be the type of the value if it's a simple value, e.g. ⟦1⟧ for single
proprioceptive value (a joint's goal position/velocity)
Note: this property should be able to be called regardless of whether the robot is connected or not.

A dictionary describing the structure and types of the feedback actions expected by the robot. Its
structure (keys) should match the structure of what is passed to :pymeth:⟦0⟧. Values for
the dict should be the type of the value if it's a simple value, e.g. ⟦1⟧ for single
proprioceptive value (a joint's goal position/velocity)
Note: this property should be able to be called regardless of whether the robot is connected or not.

Whether the teleoperator is currently connected or not. If ⟦0⟧, calling :pymeth:⟦1⟧
